body:
Here's a little adjustment to zero-pad the section locations on the statusline. The rationale here is to avoid the component resizing continuously when moving from 10-* to 1-9 (e.g., line beginning); I also added some (optional) additional whitespace padding for the separator, making it less awkward in placement and more in line with the mode indicator visual; figured I'd share it as a snippet for anyone that'd wish to have that:

```lua
local section_location = function(args)
  -- Use virtual column number to allow update when past last column
  if MiniStatusline.is_truncated(args.trunc_width) then
    return ' ' .. '%02{max([1, line(".") - 1])}' .. ' │ %02v '
  end

  -- Use `virtcol()` to correctly handle multi-byte characters
  return ' ' .. '%02{max([1, line(".") - 1])}' .. '|%02L' .. ' │ %02v|%02{max([1, virtcol("$") - 1])} '
end
```

### Before:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/135e45e8-de67-477a-ba3b-c1add69e0f2d)

### After:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/958d88f9-f8ec-4c30-9c97-c877391c19e8)

comment_data.body:
Nice little adjustment!

Couple of feedback points:
- I'd use built-in Vimscript statusline strings as possible. Hence not `string.format` in full case but something like `'%02l|%L│%02v|%-2{max([1, virtcol("$") - 1])}'`.
- Not having padding for lines is deliberate because it is not that rare to have total number of lines less than 10. In which case it introduces an unnecessary width. I feel this is not the same for number columns: it is usually either 0 or more than 10.
- I'd not recommend overriding `MiniStatusline.section_location()` directly but instead add won `local location = function() ...  end` and override the whole `MiniStatusline.content.active`.

reply_data.body:
> Out of curiosity, is there a rationale here for Vimscript vs. Lua? Is it performance? If so, is there an appropriate benchmark and/or metric I can look at?

Yeah, performance. No specific public benchmarks, though. Only that I remember doing some when writing 'mini.statusline' and concluding that using special "statusline items" (as described in `:h statusline`) was faster than some alternative solutions. 

This particular case of quite fast `string.format()` might not be super relevant here, but I'd say it is most certainly **is** better to not use `vim.fn.virtcol()` here in favor of an inline `virtcol()`. Mostly because the latter is "closer to source", so to speak.

reply_data.body:
I'd suggest to at least move `local line, virtcol = vim.fn.line, vim.fn.virtcol` to be outside of function. Otherwise it is (needlessly) executed on every statusline redraw.

That said, if you're curious for actual numbers, there is a `vim.api.nvim_eval_statusline()` which can be benchmarked. I basically use a combination of [`stat_summary()`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/74e6b722c91113bc70d4bf67249ed8de0642b20e/doc/mini-misc.txt#L212) and [`bench_time()`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/74e6b722c91113bc70d4bf67249ed8de0642b20e/doc/mini-misc.txt#L73).
